posts.caption:
Fake Christmas market booths. Real money gone. Ho ho no.

This month, scammers pretended to be B.C. holiday markets. They sent vendors invitations with real dates, table sizes and prices copied from the markets' own websites. Vendors paid by e-transfer to hold a spot. Some lost more than $1,000.

The same trick works on offices. A "supplier" emails an invoice with new bank details. It looks normal. The money goes to a scammer.

One rule stops both:
New payment details? Call first, using a number you already have. Not the one in the email.

Rushing is the scammer's best friend. A real supplier can wait for a 2-minute phone call.

Save this and share it with whoever pays the bills.

#ScamAlert #BCBusiness #VancouverBusiness #SmallBusinessTips #Cybersecurity

Plot twist: the IT guy calling you isn't your IT guy.

On Oct 28, Canada's Cyber Centre warned that scammers are calling staff at Canadian organizations, pretending to be IT support. They say there's an urgent security update, then send you to a fake sign-in page that looks like your company's. You sign in, they get in.

The fix is easy:
1. Hang up. Politely.
2. Call IT back on a number you already have.
3. Never sign in on a link someone gives you during a call.

Caller ID can be faked, so a familiar number isn't proof. A real IT person won't mind waiting two minutes. A scammer will.

Share this with your team, especially the new person.

#Cybersecurity #ScamAlert #VancouverBusiness #SmallBusinessTips #Microsoft365

Monday morning at the Liontech Zoo. 🦁

“Hi, it’s IT Support! I just need that code we sent you.”

Real IT never asks for your code. Liontech never will.

If someone calls and asks for it:
1. Hang up.
2. Call back on a number you already have.

Which coworker are you: the penguin, the gazelle or the sloth? 🐧🦌🦥

Tuesday at the Liontech Zoo. 🐘

“Hi! It’s your supplier! We have a new bank account. Please pay today.”

New bank details by email? Don’t pay yet. Call the supplier on a number you already have.

Be the elephant. Check before you pay. 🧾
